native.positiveControl: Unrestricted parent/child baseline passed inside every native run (reads of both fixtures, both write markers created and removed by exact path, child spawned and read outside bytes) and the job-owner cleanup assertions (terminateOwned, activeProcesses 0, disposed) held in both runs; the failure is the sandbox refusal, not a harness defect.

blocked.reason: The pinned Codex sandbox refuses the qualification profile: restricted read-only access (reads denied outside approved roots) requires the elevated Windows sandbox backend; this round runs unelevated by explicit constraint.

pinnedSourceEvidence.unelevatedBail: codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/lib.rs, run_windows_sandbox_capture_with_filesystem_overrides: bails with the exact observed error whenever !permissions.has_full_disk_read_access(); WRITE_RESTRICTED tokens consult restricting SIDs only for writes, so deny-read cannot be expressed unelevated.
pinnedSourceEvidence.unelevatedCapability: Full-disk-read profiles only (workspace-write style): deny-write expressible, deny-read not expressible.
pinnedSourceEvidence.elevatedRequirements: codex-rs/windows-sandbox-rs/src/elevated_impl.rs: requires dedicated sandbox logon credentials (require_logon_sandbox_creds), capability SIDs (load_or_create_cap_sids) and local ACL changes (including the null-device ACL) under an administrator context; the file contains no self-elevation step, the caller must already be elevated.

blocked.minimalAdditionalAuthorization: A specific owner decision to initialize the pinned Codex elevated Windows sandbox backend once under an administrator context: creating/using a dedicated local sandbox logon account and credentials, capability SIDs, and the local ACL changes that backend performs, then launching the qualification through the job owner elevated.
blocked.impactScope: Local machine account/ACL state only (dedicated local sandbox account, capability SIDs, local ACLs including the null device). No network access, no model calls, no production credentials, no system-wide firewall changes. The refusal is a native capability limitation, not a code defect; no assertion was deleted, no deny rule was relaxed, no full-access fallback was used, and the managed requirements (--permission-profile with --include-managed-config) were retained.
